key_insight: Leakage-controlled branching motifs from longitudinal EHRs mainly improved long-range event-timing forecasts rather than overall endpoint discrimination.
clinical_relevance: This framework could help researchers build more interpretable disease trajectory models from EHRs, but it is not yet a basis for clinical decision-making.
method: Split patients before graph construction to prevent information leakage.
Learned train-only consecutive-admission transitions and selected endpoint-specific branching motifs on validation data.
Used a time-aware Transformer with endpoint-specific cross-attention to retrieve up to 24 patient-compatible motifs per endpoint.
evidence_signal: Across five seeds, micro-AUPRC rose from 0.9330 to 0.9357 and event-time MAE fell from 676.9 to 657.7 days, with larger gains for events occurring after 730 days.
watch_item: The gains were selective, with no clear improvement in corrected survival metrics over a matched history-only model and limited benefit from replacing GNN-derived scores.
paper_title: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
